microsoft365.title: Microsoft 365 and Entra
microsoft365.description: Reads detections, incidents and audit events so a pawprint can prove your tooling actually noticed a scenario, rather than asserting it should have.

none.summary: Sign-in only. Pawprint knows who you are and nothing else.
none.note: This is the installed default. Every scope used for sign-in is user-consentable, so no admin is involved.

read.summary: Read security alerts, incidents and audit events as the signed-in user.

permissions.name: SecurityEvents.Read.All
permissions.rationale: Confirms a scenario surfaced as a Defender alert, which is the core detect-stage evidence.

permissions.name: SecurityIncident.Read.All
permissions.rationale: Correlates alerts into the incident an analyst would actually triage.

permissions.name: AuditLog.Read.All
permissions.rationale: Attributes a run to the identity that performed it when building the evidence trail.

read.note: Delegated, so the connector can never see more than the signed-in user already can. Graph security scopes require admin consent even when delegated; that is a Microsoft requirement, not a Pawprint one.

write.summary: Additionally update alert and incident status during the remediate stage.

permissions.name: SecurityEvents.ReadWrite.All
permissions.rationale: Closes or annotates the alert a scenario raised, demonstrating the full remediation loop.

permissions.name: SecurityIncident.ReadWrite.All
permissions.rationale: Resolves the incident a scenario generated so the queue is left clean.

write.note: Only needed if you want Pawprint to close what it opened. Leaving this at read and closing incidents yourself is a defensible choice.

admin.summary: Unattended, app-only access for scheduled detection polling with no user present.

permissions.name: SecurityEvents.Read.All
permissions.rationale: Allows scheduled evidence collection to continue when detection lags past the interactive session.

admin.note: Application permission is standing access that ignores Conditional Access and the signed-in user's own limits. Enable it only if you genuinely need unattended polling; delegated read covers interactive use.

azure.title: Azure subscriptions
azure.description: Deploys scenarios and reads control-plane state. Restricted to an explicit allowlist of approved subscriptions.

none.summary: No Azure access. Scenario deployment is unavailable.

read.summary: Read resource state to verify assertions, without changing anything.

permissions.name: Reader
permissions.rationale: Verifies control-plane assertions and lets the reaper find expired runs without write access.

read.note: Assigned only on subscriptions in the approved allowlist. Never at management-group or tenant root.

write.summary: Create and delete the resources a scenario needs.

permissions.name: Contributor
permissions.rationale: Creates and tears down scenario resources inside the run's own resource group.

write.note: Scoped to the run resource group, not the subscription, so the blast radius matches the run.

admin.summary: Additionally assign roles, required only by scenarios using managed-identity image pull.

permissions.name: Role Based Access Control Administrator
permissions.rationale: Grants AcrPull to the workload managed identity so images pull without stored credentials.

admin.note: This role can grant other roles, so it is a privilege-escalation path. Avoid it by publishing scenario images to a public registry, or by pre-creating the identity and assignment yourself.

cloudflare.title: Cloudflare DNS
cloudflare.description: Verifies and reconciles only the DNS records required to bind an Azure-hosted application to a Cloudflare-managed domain.

none.summary: No Cloudflare access. Custom-domain DNS remains manual.

read.summary: Verify the selected zone and its existing DNS records.

permissions.name: Zone Read
permissions.rationale: Confirms the configured hostname belongs to the intended Cloudflare zone.

permissions.name: DNS Read
permissions.rationale: Detects conflicts before any DNS record is changed.

write.summary: Additionally reconcile the Azure verification TXT record and application CNAME.

permissions.name: DNS Write
permissions.rationale: Creates or updates only the two named records required by the custom domain.

write.note: Use an account-owned service token, store it as a GitHub Environment secret named CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, and restrict its resources to the one zone. Do not use a global API key.

admin.summary: Intentionally unsupported because custom-domain automation needs no account-wide Cloudflare access.
admin.note: Use the write tier. Broader permissions add blast radius without enabling this workflow.

github.title: GitHub
github.description: Acts on repositories: reads workflow runs for evidence, opens promotion pull requests, and syncs environment variables from configuration.

none.summary: No GitHub access. Everything still works through workflows you run yourself.

read.summary: Read workflow runs and repository metadata.

permissions.name: metadata:read
permissions.rationale: Mandatory baseline permission for any GitHub App installation.

permissions.name: actions:read
permissions.rationale: Reads workflow run status so a pawprint can record the CI evidence around a run.

permissions.name: contents:read
permissions.rationale: Reads scenario manifests and configuration to validate them before deployment.

write.summary: Additionally open promotion pull requests and publish scenario images.

permissions.name: pull_requests:write
permissions.rationale: Opens and updates the dev to main promotion pull request.

permissions.name: packages:write
permissions.rationale: Publishes scenario container images so adopters can run them without provisioning a registry.

admin.summary: Additionally sync environment variables from configuration into GitHub Environments.

permissions.name: environments:write
permissions.rationale: Projects resolved configuration into GitHub Environment variables so settings stay reviewable in git.

admin.note: Environment variables can gate deployments, so write access here is effectively deployment configuration control. Sync them manually if that is too much.

evidence.detection-alerts.title: Prove a scenario surfaced as a security alert
evidence.detection-alerts.degraded: Detect-stage assertions report unknown rather than pass, and the pawprint records that no detection source was connected.

evidence.audit-attribution.title: Attribute a run to the identity that performed it
evidence.audit-attribution.degraded: The pawprint records the local operator name only, which is weaker attribution.

remediate.close-alerts.title: Close the alert a scenario raised
remediate.close-alerts.degraded: Alerts are left open for an analyst to close, and the pawprint notes that remediation was infrastructure-only.

detect.scheduled-poll.title: Keep collecting detection evidence after the session ends
detect.scheduled-poll.degraded: Detection evidence is collected only while a run is in progress, so slow detections report unknown.

verify.control-plane.title: Verify deployed resource state
verify.control-plane.degraded: Control-plane assertions report unknown and only runtime and HTTP evidence is available.

deploy.scenario.title: Deploy and tear down scenarios
deploy.scenario.degraded: Pawprint validates and renders evidence but cannot deploy anything.

deploy.managed-identity-pull.title: Pull scenario images using a managed identity
deploy.managed-identity-pull.degraded: Scenarios must use a public registry such as GHCR, which is the recommended path anyway.

reap.expired-runs.title: Automatically delete runs past their expiry
reap.expired-runs.degraded: Expired runs are reported but must be deleted by hand, so cost and exposure depend on someone remembering.

evidence.workflow-runs.title: Record CI status alongside deployment evidence
evidence.workflow-runs.degraded: The pawprint omits CI correlation and records only what the runner observed directly.

promote.pull-request.title: Open dev to main promotion pull requests from the console
promote.pull-request.degraded: Run the promotion workflow from GitHub instead; the outcome is identical.

config.sync-variables.title: Sync GitHub Environment variables from configuration
config.sync-variables.degraded: Set environment variables by hand; drift detection still reports mismatches.
